correctness.rationale: For binary words, rank-two signatures are exactly 32-bit sets of left-colour-set/colour/right-colour-set triples; the first-move EF recurrence makes the corresponding rank-three character set an exact equivalence invariant. The verified 70-letter baseline realizes 70 different rank-three characters, forcing all equivalent words to have at least 70 positions. The new 73-letter word has the identical set. Exact exhaustive C++ enumeration of all C(73,3)=62196 length-70 induced subwords finds at most 68 of the baseline 70 characters in any such subword, and none equivalent. The source code itself enumerates all triples and compares exact sets, so the evidence is a full finite computation rather than a log, sample or heuristic. A separate Python implementation confirms fingerprint equality, 961 small EF-game comparisons and 1203 sampled deletions; external independent audit is not claimed.

value.rationale: The 2017/2018 primary paper explicitly anticipated a failure of its rank-two optimal-induced-suborder theorem at rank three but did not construct one. This 73-letter example resolves that specific natural finite-model-theoretic question. The phenomenon distinguishes logical equivalence under three moves from the previously proved two-move reduction and is not a routine numerical extension. It supplies a small, fully reproducible, conceptually motivated counterexample.
